verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {claimant_primary_name}, the Claimant herein / one of the Claimants herein, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above claim petition are true and correct to my personal knowledge, and matters of legal submission are believed true on advice of counsel. promptInstructions: Draft a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, before MACT — for compensation arising from road accident.

Jurisdiction: per S.166(2) MV Act 1988 — claim may be filed at (a) Tribunal having jurisdiction over the area where accident occurred, OR (b) where the claimant resides or carries on business, OR (c) where the respondent resides.

Limitation: S.166(3) MV Act originally provided 6 months, but was DELETED by Act 54 of 1994 — no statutory bar; however, delay must be reasonably explained. The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 reintroduced a 6-month limitation effective from notified date (read with Rules) — verify current state notification. Draft on assumption of 6-month limit with condonation prayer where exceeded.
Form: Per Rule 3 of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal Rules of the respective state — typically Form 'Comp App I' / state-specific form. Particulars required are statutory minimum.
Para 1: Parties — Claimant(s), Driver (R-1), Owner (R-2), Insurer (R-3). Where pillion / passenger of offending vehicle, may need to add additional respondents.
Para 2: Jurisdiction — invoke S.166(2) ground.
Para 3-5: Accident details — date, time, place, manner. Particulars of rashness/negligence (high speed, wrong side, signal jumping, drunk driving, overloading, inadequate brakes).

Para 6: FIR details — number, date, PS, BNS sections (S.281 BNS rash driving — was IPC 279; S.106 BNS causing death by negligence — was IPC 304A; S.125 BNS rash or negligent act endangering — was IPC 336/337/338). Annex certified copy.

Para 7: Driver details and license status. Lack of valid license relevant to insurer's defence under S.149 (now S.149 read with current law) — but Pay & Recover principle of insurer applies (National Insurance v. Swaran Singh (2004) 3 SCC 297).
Para 8: Owner details and policy details.
Para 9: Insurance — verify policy was valid on date of accident; third-party insurance is mandatory under S.146 MV Act.
Para 10: Victim / deceased details — age, occupation, income with proof (salary slips, IT returns, employer certificate, self-declaration).
Para 11: Injury / death — medical particulars; for death, post-mortem; for injury, treatment record + permanent disability certificate (if applicable).
Para 12: Claimants and their relationship — for death claim, legal heirs per personal law (Hindu Succession Act 1956 / Indian Succession Act 1925 / Muslim personal law).
Para 13: Computation — apply MULTIPLIER METHOD per Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 and National Insurance Co v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680:
- Annual income calculation.
- Future prospects addition: 50% if deceased ≤40 with permanent job; 30% if 40-50; 15% if 50-60 with permanent job; for self-employed: 40% / 25% / 10%; for fixed salary: 30% / 20% / 10%.
- Personal expenses deduction: 1/3 (married + dependants), 1/2 (bachelor), graduated by family size per Sarla Verma.
- Conventional heads (Pranay Sethi): Loss of estate ₹15,000; Loss of consortium ₹40,000 per spouse; Funeral expenses ₹15,000 — to be enhanced by 10% every 3 years.
- For minor / child death — Cite Kishan Gopal v. Lala (2014) 1 SCC 244; R.K. Malik v. Kiran Pal (2009) 14 SCC 1.
- For non-earning member (housewife) — Cite Lata Wadhwa v. State of Bihar (2001) 8 SCC 197; Arun Kumar Agrawal v. National Insurance Co (2010) 9 SCC 218; Kirti v. Oriental Insurance (2021) 2 SCC 166.

Para 14: For injury claims — heads: medical expenses; loss of earning during treatment; future loss of earning capacity (based on permanent disability percent and age); pain & suffering; future medical expenses; loss of amenities; conveyance; attendant charges. Cite Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343 (permanent disability quantification).
Para 15: Pay & Recover — where insurer can plead defence (no license / breach of policy), Tribunal may direct insurer to pay and recover from owner (National Insurance v. Swaran Singh).
Para 16: Interest — 9% per annum from date of filing till realisation generally awarded.

Para 17: Reference to S.140 (no-fault liability — pre-amendment ₹50,000 for death, ₹25,000 for grievous; under MV Amendment Act 2019, S.164 provides ₹5 lakh for death and ₹2.5 lakh for grievous as no-fault).
Para 18: Reference to S.163A (structured formula — though largely superseded by Pranay Sethi computation in S.166 claims).

Annexures: FIR copy, MLC, post-mortem, hospital records, disability certificate, age proof, income proof, legal heir certificate, identity proof of claimants, RC of vehicle, DL of driver, insurance policy.
Affidavit in support mandatory.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Insurer's defences (read with current amended provisions)
Payment in case of death / grievous hurt without proof of negligence (Amendment Act 2019)
Permission to insurer to contest on owner's grounds
Rash or negligent act endangering life (was IPC 336/337/338)
Rash driving / riding on public way (was IPC 279)

filing_checklist: Claim petition in prescribed form (state MACT Rules — typically Form Comp App I)
Hospital records / discharge summary / prescriptions / bills
Income proof — salary slips / IT returns / employer certificate / self-declaration with affidavit
Photographs of accident scene / vehicle damage
Court fee / claim fee per state MACT Rules (often nominal or waived)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: victim_name and victim_age_at_accident must not be empty
accident_date must not be in future
fir_number, fir_date, police_station must not be empty
sections_charged must use BNS sections (warn if IPC 279/304A/337/338 detected)
compensation_heads must list at least one head
If claim_type = death_claim_by_legal_heirs, claimants must include all legal heirs
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format

Magma General Insurance v. Nanu Ram (2018) 18 SCC 130 — Consortium definition expanded
Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343 — Permanent disability quantification
Kishan Gopal v. Lala (2014) 1 SCC 244 — Minor death compensation
R.K. Malik v. Kiran Pal (2009) 14 SCC 1 — Child death compensation
Kirti v. Oriental Insurance (2021) 2 SCC 166 — Housewife notional income
Lata Wadhwa v. State of Bihar (2001) 8 SCC 197 — Non-earning member valuation
Reshma Kumari v. Madan Mohan (2013) 9 SCC 65 — Multiplier endorsement
